Question: Which of the US Congress members who voted to overturn the 2020 election have yet to be sentenced and imprisoned?
Answer: None. The US Constitution explicitly makes members of Congress immune for what they do and say in Congress. It’s called the “Speech and Debate clause.” It reads: The Senators and Representatives shall … be privileged from Arrest during their Attendance at the Session of their respective Houses, and in going to and returning from the same; and for any Speech or Debate in either House, they shall not be questioned in any other Place. So such a prosecution is impossible under the Constitution.

Name: Kevin Davidson
Question: What moral settings would you use on your self-driving car and why?
Answer: I don’t much care for this topic. If a driver had time to weigh moral judgments in an accident scenario, they could probably have time to avoid the accident in the first place. If humans can’t do it, then perhaps we can’t expect self-driving cars to do more than trying to avoid the accident the best it can. I drive a Tesla Model 4 with Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v12.5.1.3. It doesn’t have any moral settings, except one that has to do with speed: Automatic or strictly obey the speed limit. That’s a tough decision because where I live, most drivers regularly exceed the speed limit on some roads. One might conclude that driving the limit is dangerous. Anyhow, I would probably pick the “don’t hit anything” switch and that would be all.
